e82d84cd510e127ea76cb153a175d44ad12d761f.summary: Doron Karmi's write-up of three Konni malware campaigns observed in 2019 (January to late September). Macro-armed lure Word documents run certutil to fetch later stages, which bypass UAC, persist through the COMSysApp service, and exfiltrate data over a free FTP service. Konni is potentially linked to APT37, a North Korean espionage group. A possible overlap with the Syscon backdoor was noted but not confirmed.

e82ccde24b5b3aca43b34b4bee23e8cb83b9cc91.summary: FireEye reports a hacking group it calls NOTROBIN exploiting the Citrix NetScaler flaw CVE-2019-19781 to compromise VPN gateways. After gaining access, the actor removes known malware, installs a backdoor that works with a secret passphrase, and blocks other attackers from the flaw by deploying mitigation code. FireEye believes the actor may be collecting access to devices for a later campaign. The remaining sections of the page are unrelated news stories and are not recorded.

e8feee3a8be0dcffa6430a826b5193269142b10f.summary: Symantec reports a new Linux backdoor, Linux.Gomir, developed by the North Korean Springtail (aka Kimsuky) espionage group. It is described as a Linux version of the Windows GoBear backdoor and is linked to a campaign that delivered Troll Stealer through Trojanized installers, aimed largely at South Korean targets. The backdoor installs persistence and takes commands from a server; the report says it supports 17 commands.
